dedupe_keys.name: mapspam spatial production allocation model crop production data

description: MapSPAM publishes the outputs of the Spatial Production Allocation Model of the International Food Policy Research Institute. The model uses a cross-entropy approach to spread crop statistics from countries and subnational provinces to grid cells, giving plausible estimates of where crops are grown. Output is at about 10 by 10 km grid-cell resolution with four variables: physical area, harvested area, production and yield. The data are split by rainfed and irrigated production system and the two combined. Coverage is global for SPAM 2020, with 46 crops (about 800,000 pixels and roughly 500 million records); it is also global for 2010, 2005 and 2000, and there is a Sub-Saharan Africa release for 2017 that adds value of production. Access is free: pre-packaged downloads are split by crop, production system, variable and format (CSV and GeoTIFF, plus DBF for older releases), regional bundles and country files. The data are archived on Harvard Dataverse; SPAM 2020 v2.2 was updated on 5 May 2026 (doi 10.7910/DVN/SWPENT). Use falls under the IFPRI Datasets Terms of Use, which treat the data as global public goods with unrestricted public access; the Dataverse record carries no separate licence field. Caveats: the grid values are modelled allocations, not observations, and releases for different years use different crop lists and methods. For simulation it gives the spatial exposure of crop production to floods, droughts and heat, and the production baseline for food-supply disruption studies. Related catalogue records include EarthStat, FAO GAEZ and FAOSTAT.
